meaning: Structural proof-obligation registry, not proof validity

obligations.statement: Each published UNSAT trace used in the fixed-outdegree-six Caccetta-Häggkvist computation is accepted by an independent proof-trace checker on its exact published input.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The external fixed-r=6 proof corpus is already reported in the literature; this repository has not independently replayed the 438 MB corpus. Replay would reproduce a claim, not establish novelty.
obligations.falsifier: One reported UNSAT certificate fails an independent checker, or a published input digest differs from the input actually replayed.
obligations.next_action: Acquire the cited proof corpus with exact hashes; replay every proof trace with an independently pinned checker and preserve the input-to-trace manifest.

obligations.statement: The published hand reductions and case split for minimum outdegree six cover every digraph admissible under the stated restricted theorem without dropping an exceptional case.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: An accepted UNSAT trace does not prove that the originating CNFs exhaust the mathematical cases. The published fixed-r=6 argument is not a resolution of the unrestricted Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture.
obligations.falsifier: A digraph admissible under the restricted statement is not represented by any certified case, or a reduction changes an outdegree/cycle quantifier.
obligations.next_action: Write a finite, numbered reduction ledger from the original quantified statement to each CNF family; check edge cases and the exact r=6, n and cycle-bound conventions.

obligations.statement: The claimed fixed-outdegree-six Caccetta-Häggkvist result follows from the published exhaustive case split and the independently replayed UNSAT proof traces, for exactly the parameter range and graph conventions stated in the source.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: This is a conditional audit target for an already claimed restricted result, not a new solution and not a promotion to the full Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture.
obligations.falsifier: Either a traced case is not certified or an admissible case is absent from the reduction; failure of either dependency blocks this conclusion.
obligations.next_action: After the trace and reduction obligations are discharged, independently check the implication from both premises to the exact restricted theorem.

obligations.statement: For union-closed families over a five-element ground set, a canonical encoding is constant on each relabeling orbit and separates distinct relabeling orbits.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The existing n=4 census and its 366 relabeling orbits are known finite benchmark data; an n=5 canonicalization lemma is a proposed structural step, not established.
obligations.falsifier: Two relabeling-equivalent families receive different codes, or two inequivalent families receive the same code.
obligations.next_action: A paper proof of the minimum S5 orbit invariant and implementation are in research/M075_CANONICAL.md and scripts/frankl_canonical.py. Obtain independent mathematical and statement-fidelity review before discharge; the existing n4 mine provides a second finite cross-check.

obligations.statement: A canonical family generator over a five-element ground set emits exactly one union-closed family per relabeling orbit without enumerating all 2^(2^5) set systems.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: No speedup claim follows from the n=4 orbit table; completeness and no-duplication are separate from empirical speed.
obligations.falsifier: An omitted relabeling orbit, a duplicated orbit, an emitted non-union-closed family, or a fallback that enumerates every set system.
obligations.next_action: The n5 labeled full-support count 2747402 and n5 orbit count 28960 now have independent closure-pruned and Burnside checkers (research/M075_CANONICAL.md and M075_BURNSIDE.md), with a written exact-once proof. Obtain independent scope and mathematical reviews before discharge. Next performance goal is canonical augmentation pruning noncanonical partial states, not repeating known finite enumerations.

obligations.statement: The cited 42-vertex two-colouring of the complete graph has neither a red K5 nor a blue K5, as checked directly from its published adjacency data.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: A known K42 witness would reproduce a published Ramsey lower bound. It does not yield an upper bound or determine R(5,5).
obligations.falsifier: An explicit five-vertex monochromatic clique in the imported colouring, or a vertex/edge count inconsistent with K42.
obligations.next_action: The cited 328-graph K42 catalog has a pinned offline, dual-checker reproduction (scripts/verify_mckay.py). Obtain genuinely independent mathematical and statement-scope review of that exact replay before discharging this known-witness node; a K43 counterexample or full upper-bound proof remains a separate open target.

obligations.statement: There is an explicitly named family of p-blocks, with a fixed defect-group isomorphism type outside the published order-100 census, for which the number of Alperin weights equals the number of irreducible Brauer characters.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The named-group probe through A5, and the published verification for every group of order at most 100, are known finite benchmarks. A restricted block-family lemma is not established here.
obligations.falsifier: A block in the named family whose independently recomputed weight count differs from its Brauer-character count, or a definition of the family that collapses into the order-100 census.
obligations.next_action: Name the defect-group isomorphism type and the ambient groups, write the exact weight-count lemma, and state the finite certificate an independent checker would accept.

obligations.statement: There is an explicit upper bound B on the least prime p in a Goldbach partition of every even n in a named infinite residue class, such that B is not already implied by the published 4*10^18 verification.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Even Goldbach through 4*10^18 and the ternary Goldbach theorem are known; the certified mine of record least primes through 20,000 is a reproduction, not a new bound.
obligations.falsifier: An even n in the named class whose least Goldbach prime exceeds B, or a proof that B follows from already-published verification alone.
obligations.next_action: Name the residue class and the candidate bound B; test it against the twelve record pairs in the goldbach_growth mine; do not extend the verified range toward 4*10^18.

obligations.statement: There is a polynomial identity that produces positive-integer solutions of 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z for every prime n = 1 (mod 24) with 4x - n equal to 3, or separately for every such prime with 4x - n equal to 7.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Classical Mordell-type identities leave quadratic-residue classes uncovered; the straus_patterns mine through 8000 is a certified table, not a symbolic identity.
obligations.falsifier: A prime n = 1 (mod 24) in the claimed residue for which the proposed identity fails to give positive integers, or a citation showing the identity is already classical.
obligations.next_action: Prove a symbolic identity for residue 3 or residue 7; treat the certified table as a guide, not as the lemma.

obligations.statement: For one primitive Dirichlet character of conductor 3 or 5, the interval-arithmetic argument principle certifies N(T) matching Hardy-style critical-line sign changes up to an explicit height, with root number and gamma factor checked independently.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The existing chi_4 certificate to height 17 is a known-method reproduction; GRH concerns all characters, so one more character tests the reusable contour, not the conjecture.
obligations.falsifier: A mismatch between the certified argument count and the number of critical-line sign changes, or an incorrect root number/gamma-factor convention.
obligations.next_action: Replay a published primitive character modulo 3 or 5 with independent Gauss-sum and zero-count checks; document that this is known mathematics, not GRH progress.

obligations.statement: The finite graph cited in the 2026 Hadwiger claim review has a certified chromatic-number lower bound t and an independently checked certificate that no K_t minor exists.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Chromatic number at most 6 is already settled by Robertson–Seymour–Thomas. The extractability audit (research/M071_M073_WITNESSES.md) found an existential/asymptotic Lean family with no published finite adjacency list; comparator acceptance alone cannot discharge this node.
obligations.falsifier: The graph admits a K_t minor, its chromatic lower bound fails an independent check, or the encoding does not match the claimed manuscript object.
obligations.next_action: Obtain an explicit finite graph with independent chromatic and minor certificates, or specialist reviews of the existential proof. Do not treat the frozen no_explicit_finite_graph ledger entry as a discharged witness.

obligations.statement: The finite host G cited in the 2026 Sidorenko claim review, together with the stated bipartite pattern H, satisfies t(H,G) < t(K2,G)^e(H) under exact rational homomorphism densities computed by two independent methods.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The extractability audit reconstructed pattern H (35 vertices, 66 edges) in data/reference/sidorenko_faces.json; the claimed host G remains unpublished. Small unweighted hosts already checked here are not that object.
obligations.falsifier: Exact densities that obey the Sidorenko inequality, a mismatch with the manuscript construction, or a host that cannot be reconstructed from the cited data.
obligations.next_action: Derive or obtain the claimed host G and compute exact densities with two independent methods, or keep the pattern_reconstructed_host_missing gap. Pattern H alone does not discharge this node.

obligations.statement: There is a deck invariant, strictly stronger than the pair (degree sequence, triangle count), that separates every pair of non-isomorphic graphs on at most 6 vertices that the current mine leaves colliding.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Computer verification of reconstruction already reaches at least 11 vertices; degree-plus-triangles through 5 vertices with 20 collisions at 6 vertices is a certified reproduction, not a new theorem.
obligations.falsifier: Two non-isomorphic 6-vertex graphs with identical proposed invariants and identical decks, or a proof that the invariant is equivalent to degree sequence plus triangles.
obligations.next_action: Name the invariant, recompute it on the twenty excess graphs at 6 vertices, and state the finite certificate format.

obligations.statement: Every finite poset of width at least 3 that is not a chain has an incomparable pair with balance in [1/3, 2/3], for a named restricted class (for example bounded height) not already settled by Linial's width-2 theorem.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Linial settled width 2; published verification reaches 11 elements; the poset_balance mine's tight examples on at most 6 elements all have width 2.
obligations.falsifier: A non-chain poset of width at least 3 in the named class whose every incomparable pair has balance strictly outside [1/3, 2/3], with two independent exact extension counts.
obligations.next_action: Name the restricted class and write the balance lemma; do not enlarge the width-2 census.

obligations.statement: Under the stabilizer of the standard basis, every orbit of 4-tuples of bases of GF(2)^4 has an explicit representative together with a grid certificate or an exhaustive negative certificate.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Chan (1995) covers rank at most 3; GF(2)^4 is the next finite case and is not yet orbit-reduced in this repository.
obligations.falsifier: An orbit with neither a valid grid nor a complete negative certificate, or a stabilizer quotient that drops an orbit.
obligations.next_action: Implement the orbit quotient so GF(2)^4 becomes exhaustive and store one certificate per orbit.

obligations.statement: A cited published exact decomposition of the <3,3,3> matrix-multiplication tensor of rank 23 (or another named small-format scheme) replays on the repository tensor checker with matching bilinear identities.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Small-format ranks cannot beat laser-method bounds below 2.372; replaying a published decomposition is certificate infrastructure, not progress toward omega = 2.
obligations.falsifier: A bilinear identity failure under the checker, or a scheme whose published rank does not match the imported tensors.
obligations.next_action: Import one published exact decomposition onto the existing checker; do not launch a flip-graph search as the next step.

obligations.statement: For an explicitly locked field characteristic, circuit shape, degree bound and oracle model, a deterministic polynomial-size hitting set hits every nonzero circuit in that class.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The restricted GF(2) degree-≤3 ≤20-gate black-box class is locked in-repo. A hitting set for that class would be a restricted lemma, not a resolution of unrestricted PIT.
obligations.falsifier: A nonzero circuit in the locked class that vanishes at every hitting-set point, or a lock paragraph that leaves characteristic, shape, degree or oracle unspecified.
obligations.next_action: Class lock is in research/M088_LOCK.md. Implement the exact falsifier (nonzero circuit vanishing on a proposed hitting set) against that lock; independent mathematical and statement-fidelity review still required before discharge.

obligations.statement: A published exact SIC fiducial in some dimension d with 4 <= d <= 8 replays under exact arithmetic in the extended cyclotomic engine, with all equiangularity identities certified.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Exact fiducials beyond d = 3 are published; floating-point SICs are not proofs. Replaying them tests the number-field engine, not a uniform existence theorem.
obligations.falsifier: A failed Gram identity, a missing vector under the stated construction, or a number-field encoding that does not match the published fiducial.
obligations.next_action: Extend the cyclotomic engine to the needed fields and replay published exact fiducials for d <= 8 with an independent overlap checker.

obligations.statement: For each q <= 9, the maximum size of a 4-arc in PG(3,q) computed by the frame-fixing engine matches a cited published value, with exact determinant checks.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The MDS conjecture is proved for prime q (Ball 2012); k = 3 is the Segre–Bose range. Reproducing known maxima for small q is not a new bound.
obligations.falsifier: An n-arc exceeding the cited maximum with verified determinants, or a search that misses a published arc.
obligations.next_action: Generalise the arc engine to PG(3,q) with 5-point frames and reproduce known maximum arc sizes for q <= 9.

obligations.statement: Hadamard matrices of orders 116, 156 and 172 are constructed by the symmetry-reduced Williamson or Goethals–Seidel engines and pass exact orthogonality certificates.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: These orders are constructed in the literature; the open case begins at order 668. Closing engine gaps is reproduction, not a new existence theorem.
obligations.falsifier: A constructed matrix failing H H^T = n I, or a symmetry reduction that omits a published construction class needed for these orders.
obligations.next_action: Add multiplier-group symmetry for Williamson n = 29 and Goethals–Seidel arrays for 156 and 172; document the first order no implemented method reaches.

obligations.statement: A published partial nonexistence restriction for a projective plane of order 12 (for example a prescribed collineation class) is reproduced as a SAT instance with an independently checked DRAT/LRAT proof.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Order-10 nonexistence required a massive computation; unconstrained order-12 search is out of reach. Replaying a published restriction is not a decision of existence.
obligations.falsifier: A SAT encoding whose models are not planes of the stated class, a proof that fails an independent checker, or a restriction weaker than the cited published one.
obligations.next_action: Encode order-12 planes with a prescribed collineation as SAT with DRAT output, starting from cases the literature already excludes.

obligations.statement: For every 1-2 metric or vertex-weighted metric on at most 8 vertices, the exact Held–Karp integrality gap is at most the published graphic-metric maximum for that n, or an explicit gap-maximising instance is certified by LP duality and brute-force tour search.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Graphic metrics through 7 vertices are a certified reproduction of known small-n gaps; extending vertices inside that published range is not the next experiment.
obligations.falsifier: A metric whose certified Held–Karp value and optimal tour give a gap above both the claimed bound and the published graphic maximum, or a duality certificate that fails independent replay.
obligations.next_action: Extend from graphic metrics to 1-2 and vertex-weighted metrics; enumerate extreme points of the subtour polytope at n = 8.

obligations.statement: There is a named Newton-polygon family of plane polynomial maps, with coefficients in an explicit ring and degree outside Moh's degree-100 bound, for which the Jacobian conjecture is proved or an exact counterexample certificate is given.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: Wang covers degree <= 2 and Moh covers plane degree <= 100; enumerating degree-4 maps with coefficients in {-1,0,1} is refused as dominated.
obligations.falsifier: A family that collapses into degree <= 100 over C, or a Jacobian-nonvanishing map in the family with a certified missing inverse under Gabber's bound.
obligations.next_action: Name one Newton-polygon family outside the degree-100 bound and state the coefficient ring before any search; do not enumerate degree-4 maps with coefficients in {-1,0,1}.

obligations.statement: There is an explicit zero-free region or verified analytic statement about zeta that is not implied by plugging any height covered by published critical-line computations into a known explicit formula.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The interval verifier to T = 36 is far below Platt–Trudgian; extending that tiny height inside the published range is refused as dominated.
obligations.falsifier: A proof that the proposed statement follows from existing published zero computations alone, or a counterexample inside the claimed region.
obligations.next_action: Do not prioritize extending T = 36. Identify a mathematically new zero-free region, explicit bound, or verified statement not implied by existing computations.

obligations.statement: The 2026 claimed finite presentation of a torsion-free group G and elements a,b in F_2[G] satisfy ab=1 and ba≠1 under two independent group-ring multiplications on the exact published supports.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The OpenAI math manuscript claims a counterexample to direct finiteness; this node only asks for independent replay. Matching the registered statement is not novelty credit.
obligations.falsifier: A multiplication trace where ab≠1, or ba=1, or the presentation/supports disagree with the cited source.
obligations.next_action: Import or rebuild an independent group-ring checker; replay the claimed presentation and products; preserve input digests.

obligations.statement: Given an independently replayed M044 witness over F_2, the Elek–Szabó theorem applies with exactly the stated hypotheses and implies that the same finitely presented group is nonsofic.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: M044 and M049 share one manuscript; a second PDF is not a second proof. The upstream Lean comparator does not by itself assert nonsoficity.
obligations.falsifier: A missing hypothesis in the soficity implication for the claimed field, or a failure of the M044 dependency.
obligations.next_action: After O-M044-01, write an implication checklist for Elek–Szabó over F_2 on that presentation; do not open a duplicate witness search.

obligations.statement: Every finite width-three poset consisting of a chain and three pairwise incomparable outsiders, each incomparable with at least one chain element, has balance constant at least 11/28; the constant is sharp.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The unrestricted one-third–two-thirds conjecture is open. The previously proposed chain-plus-two 4/11 bound is a different class; finite verification and source searches do not establish historical novelty or independent mathematical acceptance.
obligations.falsifier: A poset meeting the exact hypotheses with all incomparable-pair probabilities outside [11/28,17/28], a gap-coordinate counterexample, or an earlier source proving the same bound.
obligations.next_action: Prove the all-orders insertion-gap reduction and exact finite residual bound, independently replay the sharp example and attack the 67392 normalized cases; then obtain specialist and novelty review.

obligations.statement: Every finite width-five poset consisting of a chain and five pairwise incomparable outsiders, each incomparable with at least one chain element, has balance constant at least 3/8; a 13-element witness has balance 2/5.
obligations.prior_art_boundary: The unrestricted 1/3–2/3 conjecture remains open. The earlier chain-plus-four 25/61 candidate is a different class; 2026 large-width asymptotic theorems and finite order-14 computations do not by themselves establish this all-orders fixed-width-five bound. Historical novelty and independent mathematical acceptance are not established.
obligations.falsifier: A valid chain-plus-five width-five interval tuple with balance below 3/8; a missed normalized interval multiset; disagreement between the two exact recurrences or the relation-matrix checker; a flawed gap-atom cutoff; or a primary prior-art theorem covering this class and constant.
obligations.next_action: Independently audit the all-orders gap-atom and Helly reductions, the 40,355,371-case exact dual recurrence and 1405-extension witness in research/M079_CHAIN_PLUS_FIVE.md; obtain external mathematical and historical-novelty review. Do not change solved status.
